title: Hypoglycemic Glucose Reperfusion and Axonal Self Destruction

teenKit.tldr: When paramedics instantly flood a starving brain with a massive dose of sugar, it accidentally triggers a biochemical self-destruct mechanism that destroys the tissue. This chilling medical paradox happens when cells weaponize their own cellular fuel to tear themselves apart from the inside.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how our own cells pull the plug on themselves is completely rewriting emergency medicine and revealing unexpected links between sudden brain trauma and slow-moving chemotherapy side effects.
keyTakeaways: A life-saving intervention like a concentrated sugar injection can paradoxically become a weapon that permanently dismantles brain tissue during a severe metabolic crash.
Internal metabolic sabotage happens when cells actively and deliberately execute themselves from the inside out instead of dying from external physical trauma.
Both acute brain crises and slow peripheral nerve damage share a single microscopic link: they hinge on a vital cellular fuel molecule called NAD+, which the cell tears apart.
